newsitem.title: USA: TransAmerican new junk bonds get warm reception.
newsitem.headline: TransAmerican new junk bonds get warm reception.

text.p: Investors gave a warm reception on Thursday to more than $1.5 billion (principal amount) in new junk bonds issused by TransAmerican Energy Corp, market sources said.

The bonds' prices rose soon after the deal priced on Thursday, suggesting strong demand, they said. The company's $475 million in 11 1/2 percent senior secured notes due 02 were quoted 102 1/2-102 3/4 after being priced at par. Its $1.13 billion (principal amount) of 13 percent zero coupon bonds due 02 traded as high as 79 and were most recently quoted around 78, after being priced at 77.6779, a trader said.
Jefferies & Co Inc was the sole underwriter of the mega-junk bond offering from TransAmerican, a holding company owned by oil and gas mogul John Stanley.

The bulk of the proceeds from the offering will be used to refinance over $1 billion in outstanding high-yield bonds from TransAmerican's two operating subsidiaries--TransAmerican Refining Corp and TransTexas Gas Corp.
A Jefferies official confirmed a large number of buyers of the new bonds were also investors in the outstanding debt.
"Stanley has a good record with bondholders over the past five years. He has earned their trust," he said.

But analysts and traders were quick to point out investors were attracted to the juicy yields on the bonds, which compensated investors for their highly speculative nature. The deal was rated B3/B-plus.
"This is a hot market and clearly there was quite a bit of demand for bonds with such a high coupon," said Erik Dybesland, high-yield energy analyst at Bear Stearns & Co.
A trader who was not connected with the deal said, "People wanted something big and cheap and that's what they got."
He noted investors were also attracted to the liquidity of the large offering.
Dybesland said some investors would likely buy the bonds in order to meet their portfolio benchmark targets.

He noted that because of its large size, the TransAmerican deal will feature prominently in high-yield bond indexes which are used by many institutional investors to gauge their portfolio's performance.
Dybesland added that the cash-paying bonds, because of their high coupons, were likely to attract interest from managers of new collaterized bond obligations as well.
A TransAmerican spokesman did not return calls about the offering.
